articleTitle: IEE Seminar on 'Quality Through Integrated Process Management' (Digest No.167)
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Quality Through Integrated Process Management
IEE Seminar on Quality Through Integrated Process Management
abstract: In 1987, International Computers Ltd. (ICL) defined as one of its key strategies for survival 'to become a household name for quality and customer care'. Major worldwide programmes were introduced to develop a new culture into the company whereby every employee would come to regard customer satisfaction as paramount. The author describes how a quality improvement process was implemented across the company and this was subsequently complemented by an integrated process management programme to achieve registration to ISO9001 worldwide.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Quality Through Integrated Process Management
abstract: British Telecom (BT) runs a large and complex operation delivering customer service from hundreds of locations across the UK and now increasingly across the globe. Such service is delivered through a chain of activities across a number of different functional and organisational units. Clearly, to be successful, improvement activities have to be well thought out and integrated in a highly disciplined manner. Here, the author describes how process management is now seen as providing that discipline.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Case study: how Akzo Chemicals runs MTQ (managing total quality)
publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Quality Through Integrated Process Management
abstract: Many organisations practice TQM (total quality management), but consistency in definitions within one company is important. In Akzo Chemicals, they call it MTQ, managing total quality, a process model obtained from 3M Quality Management Services. Here, the author presents an overview of some of the action which Akzo Chemicals have taken in order to make this quality process come alive within their company.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Quality Through Integrated Process Management
abstract: Western economic performance is primarily the result of financial oriented management thinking. Here the author describes how, by contrast, Far Eastern (notable Japanese) economic performance results from concentration on continual improvement through process oriented management. Financial thinking sees earnings per share as the barometer of business success. Process thinking however sees added value per unit payroll cost as a more important measure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Seminar on Quality Through Integrated Process Management
abstract: The author examines learning process improvement in deliberate contrast to teaching process improvement. He sees teaching as an event 'done' by one to another, whereas learning is a self managed process that may need some teaching input. The application of such ideas to the improvement of work processes is then discussed. Operator competence, global competition and process progress monitoring are also touched upon.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
